## Pass 1

Changes (unit · field · severity · what was wrong · what was done). Units are numbered from 0 as in units.json.

- U10 · words[imḏw·k] glyphs/reading/say/morph · major · N26 (the two-humped mountain) was given tr "dw" and the word read imdw from Budge's ṭ. N26's value is ḏw (Budge's ṭu "mountain"), and Budge's slips follow the signs · N26 tr → "ḏw", reading → imḏw·k, say → imedjuk, lemma imdw → imḏw.
- U10 · l / i · major · "advocate(?)" for a word no lexicon gives was Budge's 1895 guess carried into l and i · word left as a gap: l "I · […]-your · Osiris", i "I am your […], Osiris." (same device as weighing-of-the-heart unit 10).
- U13 · words[imḏw·k] glyphs/reading/say/morph · major · same as U10 · same fix.
- U13 · l / i / n · major · same as U10 ("advocate(?)", "I(?)") · l "I · […]-your · Horus", i "I am your […], Horus."; note rewritten to point back to l. 8.
- U10 · n · minor · ink written n-w-man was hedged as doubtful, though every other sentence of the speech begins with ink and the n-w spells out the pot nw that writes in in ink · note now opens "The papyrus writes n and w with the kneeling man, without the k (Budge: nuà); read ink 'I'."; (?) dropped from "I" in l. Rest of the note rewritten: the sign values im + ḏw, the loaf t not read, Budge's àmṭu/temṭu, why the gap.
- U8 · words[ḏꜣḏꜣt] glyph W24 · minor · the pot was coded comp "ꜣ", but W24 does not write ꜣ, so it cannot be a complement of ꜣ; the published weighing of the heart codes the same pot det/unread · role → det, tr "". Note: "is not read, as in the weighing of the heart: the pot does not write ꜣ." (The introduction to Spell 125 apparently has comp ꜣ. Pass 2 or the owner should settle the two published parts.)
- U7 · n · minor · reading ꜥḥꜣ departs from Budge's āba (b, not ḥ) and the note did not say why · added: no sign in the pair can be identified as either consonant; ꜥḥꜣ is usually written with arms holding a shield and a weapon, and the round-topped slab may be a misdrawn shield. The reading is still marked doubtful.
- U5 · n · minor · over-hedged: "That gives no clear sentence, but the reading 'says' is not sure either". in + noun after quoted words is the regular "says N", and the red ends on in · replaced with "Budge renders àn 'behold', which in does not mean; in with a noun after quoted words is the regular way of writing 'says N'." Also added that im·i may as well be "in me" as "with me".
- U3 · n · minor · claimed Budge gives Ani the hand-to-mouth figure "in this part, not the plain seated man of earlier plates". The packet says it is the glyph Budge always uses for Ani; the earlier parts only code it differently · now "The earlier parts code the same figure in Ani's name A51 or A1; here it is coded A2 from its shape".
- U14 · i · minor · "gone forth(?)": "forth" is pri, not sbi · now "I have gone(?) for your name."
- U8 · n · style · the doubled demonstrative was corrected in i, but the note did not open with the slip formula · now opens "The papyrus writes the demonstrative twice, nn n nn nṯrw; read it once, nn n nṯrw, as in line 8." The surplus sentence was removed.
- U6 · n · style · the enma slip was mid-note · moved to open the note: "The papyrus writes n before m (water n, then Aa15 with a stroke; Budge: enma, marked '(sic)'); read m 'in'."
- U11 · words[nṯrw] glyph R8 · style · the first of three flags was coded log; published parts (weighing, hymn to Osiris) code the triple R8 as phon nṯr + det + det · role → phon.
- U16 · n · style · added that imy is masculine too, where ḥwt would want imyt, so both forms leave wr ambiguous between ḥwt and sr.

Considered and refused:
- U5 in = "says" vs "behold": kept "says". in + noun after a quotation is regular Middle Egyptian, the red ends on in as it ends on ḏd in before a name, and "behold" is not a meaning of in. The hedge is reduced, not removed, because im·i stays unclear.
- U5 im·i (lemma m, ·i): correct. Known m lists "im before a suffix (im·i …)". The "(?)" stays, because how it joins the sentence is unclear.
- U0 ḥꜣt-ꜥ as a new key instead of ḥꜣt: kept. It is a fixed compound, like ḥwt-nṯr, which has its own key. F4 log ḥꜣt + D36 phon ꜥ agrees with the reading.
- U2 ḏdt as a feminine passive participle "what is (to be) said", alternative ḏd·t(w): grammatically sound and both noted, so kept. Lemma ḏd covers ḏdt per known.
- U7/U14 ꜥḥꜣ with O26 + N29: reading kept as doubtful. Budge's English and the sense support "fight", and the codes cannot change. O26 is phon ꜥḥꜣ with N29 det because the pair is treated as one unidentified sign: acceptable, and the note says so.
- U6 "enma (sic)" read m: kept. No reading of n + m gives a sentence; Budge's sic marks the papyrus's own writing.
- U8/U11 nn spelled n + adze nw + w (Budge ennu), with tr chunks giving "nnw" while the reading is nn: kept. The reading gives the word meant, and the note names the spelling. It is like ḫftyw with the vulture.
- U8 doubled nn: kept as one surplus word, read once in i. l still shows both words in the papyrus's order, which is what l is for.
- U12 smꜣyw from a written smꜣꜥ: slip accepted. The knife classifier and the sense require "slay", and the note opens with the formula. The surplus Aa11/D36 keep their phon tr, as the published hymn keeps phon t on the unread t's of wnn·f. House practice allows both this and det/unread.
- U12 ḫnr "restrain" (Budge χenrà "shut up"): the signs give ḫ-n-r plus an unread reed, the sense fits, and the participle label is right. Kept, as a new key.
- U14 sbi·n·i "I have gone(?)": the signs (s, b, y, walking legs, n, ·i) give sbi, which is in known with "go, pass". Budge's "made the defeat" is not in the signs. Doubt kept.
- U16 wr with ḥwt vs sr: wr and imy are both masculine. sr would agree, but the scribe often drops the feminine t (weighing: "the feminine t is not written"), so it is ambiguous. Kept i "the great Mansion of the Noble" with the note giving "Mansion of the Great Noble"; only the imy point was added.
- U5 reading ḥḥ with lemma nḥḥ (n not written): kept, because it is identical to the published hymn to Osiris.
- U8/U15 ḫftyw·f with the vulture G1 tr ꜣ while the reading has -y: kept. Signs keep their own value and the note says the vulture stands for the ending. Budge χefta agrees with the signs.
- U9 the claim that the surplus hand in wḏꜥ is "the same spelling as in the weighing of the heart": verified (weighing wḏꜥ·n: G43 I10 D46/det Aa21), so it stands.
- U6/U8/U10… ink with W24 tr "in": the note explains it; kept.
- say forms ahaeni / sebieni: they follow the published wedjaeni / djedeni / iieni pattern. hrw heru, iwnw Iunu, imntt imentet, ẖrt-nṯr kheret-netjer, Hut-ser and the god names all match the published parts.
- U6 "the hymn to Ra sets Thoth beside Maat", U7 "the same pair stands among the classifiers of ṯmsw in the address of Spell 125", U8 "as in the address of Spell 125" (nn spelling): these are outside the files this pass was allowed to read, so they were not verified and not changed. Pass 2 should confirm them.
- No Budge-isms in l/i ("saith", "homage", "triumphant", "Àmentet": none); "thy" appears only inside quotations of Budge in notes.
- ꜣḫt as an adjective under lemma ꜣḫ with a gloss override; ḥr "for, on behalf of" override; in "to say" override: each is a sense of an existing key, so the glosser should handle it under __broaden__, not with a new key.

Re-check: the concatenated glyph codes of units.json equal the packet's sequence (381 signs), all 106 q values equal the packet's, and restored flags stay on both glyphs of wꜥ, l. 8.

## Pass 2

Changes (unit/entry · field · severity · what was wrong · what was done).

- U1 · n / l / i · minor · sꜣḫw was called an infinitive ("the next four words are infinitives used as nouns"; "It is the causative of ꜣḫ"). The w ending makes it the plural noun sꜣḫw 'glorifications'; the infinitive of a causative of a 2-radical verb is plain sꜣḫ · note now "nouns of action", and "a plural noun from sꜣḫ 'glorify', the causative of ꜣḫ"; l "glorifying" → "glorifications"; i "of raising up and glorifying" → "of raising up and glorification".
- U0 · n · minor · "a compound noun, literally 'the front of the arm'" is an invented etymology: the sense of ꜥ in ḥꜣt-ꜥ is not clear · now "a compound noun used for the start of a book or a list; what the arm adds to ḥꜣt 'front' is not clear."
- U6 · n · minor · "the hymn to Ra sets Thoth beside Maat": the hymn (units 14, 26) has Thoth and Maat together on either side of the sun in his bark, not Thoth set beside Maat · now "in which the hymn to Ra places Thoth and Maat on either side of the sun."
- U8 · n · minor · "nn … water n, the adze nw and the chick w, as in the address of Spell 125": the address writes n + adze + pot nw + chick (unit 45) or n + adze + pot (unit 95), never this three-sign form · now "a shorter form of the spelling in the address of Spell 125, which adds the pot nw, as line 8 does here." (U11's "as in the address" is exact and stays.)
- U7 · n · minor · U15 called "the classifier of force": U15 is the sledge (tm); the published address says the sign printed U15 stands for the forearm with a stick · now "A low sign printed like the sledge (U15) follows; as in the address of Spell 125, it stands for the forearm with a stick, the classifier of force, and is not read."
- U12 · n · minor · same ("the low sign of force (U15)") · now "the low sign printed like the sledge (U15), for the classifier of force, as in line 5."
- U10 · n · minor · the ink slip note did not say that the n-w-man writing comes twice (l. 8 and l. 10), which weighs against a one-off slip · added: "The same writing comes again in line 10, so it may be this scribe's habit rather than a single slip; the word meant is ink either way."
- U8 · n · style · ḏꜣḏꜣt pot: the note said only that the pot is not read; it now says why a reader might take it for ꜣ and why it is not: "stands where the vulture ꜣ, the complement of ḏꜣ, would be expected; but the pot does not write ꜣ and the word is complete without it, so it is not read, as in the weighing of the heart." Coding unchanged (W24 det, tr "").
- U8, U15 · l · style · "his-enemies" put the suffix before the noun, against the Egyptian order that l shows and the published parts use ("heart-my", "beauty · your") · → "enemies-his".
- U16 · n · style · imy was described twice in two consecutive sentences · merged into one sentence.
- gloss ḥꜣt-ꜥ · minor · "noun f.; literally 'the front of the arm'": invented etymology · now "beginning, start, especially of a book or list (compound noun of ḥꜣt 'front' and ꜥ 'arm'; ḥꜣt-ꜥ m 'the beginning of')".
- gloss sꜣḫ · minor · sꜣḫw labelled "infinitive used as a noun" · now "(verb; causative of ꜣḫ); sꜣḫw 'glorifications', the recitations that do this for the dead (noun, plural)".
- gloss sṯs · style · part-specific infinitive remark and a Budge spelling on a plain verb (conventions keep Budge's spelling for names) · now "to raise up, lift; to extol, praise (verb; causative of ṯs 'raise')".
- gloss ꜥḥꜣ · minor · "Budge: āba" given as if Budge's spelling of the lemma (his āba is his reading of this part's doubtful signs; ꜥḥꜣ would be āḥa in his letters) and the part-specific doubt and the sḏm·n·f example were in the general entry · now "to fight (verb)"; the doubt stays in the U7/U14 notes.
- gloss smꜣꜥ-ḫrw · style · "participle 'who make …'" is part-specific · now "(verb; causative of mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'true of voice'; smꜣꜥ-ḫrw N r 'vindicate N against')".
- gloss imḏw · minor · "a title or office" claimed more than the signs show · now "a word for a person or a god, perhaps a title; reading and meaning unknown (noun, with the classifiers of a man and a god; Budge: àmṭu, 'advocate', a guess from the sense)".
- gloss ḫnr · style · part-specific participle and a Budge spelling on a plain verb · now "to restrain, hold back, shut in (verb)".

ḏꜣḏꜣt across the published parts: the weighing of the heart (unit 3) codes the pot W24 det with empty tr ("not read"); the introduction to Spell 125 (unit 9) codes it phon "ꜣ" and opens its note "The papyrus writes ḏꜣ-nw-t-ḏꜣ-s; read ḏꜣḏꜣt", saying the pot "stands for ꜣ". The weighing's coding is the more defensible: a sign's tr is its own value, the pot never has the value ꜣ, and the U28 drill already carries ḏꜣ, so the word is complete without it. This part keeps det / "" (as pass 1 left it) and the note now explains it. The introduction is inconsistent with both and should be recoded by the owner (W24 det, tr ""), which this pass may not edit.

Verified and kept:
- U7 "the same pair stands among the classifiers of ṯmsw 'harm' in the address of Spell 125": verified (address unit 29: ṯmsw … O26/det N29/det G37/det Z2/det).
- U11 "nn … water n, the adze nw (approximate), the pot nw and the chick w, as in the address of Spell 125": verified (address unit 45, same four signs, same roles).
- U8 second nn "the spelling in the weighing of the heart": verified (weighing unit 21: M22 M22 N35 N35).
- U9 ḏdt "U28 … for ḏ as in the introduction to Spell 125": verified (introduction unit 5, ḏdt·i U28/phon/ḏ). U9 wḏꜥ with the surplus hand "as in the weighing": verified (weighing unit 30).
- U16 ḥwt-sr "named in the hymn to Ra": verified (hymn unit 18; same coding O6/phon/ḥwt A21/log/sr).
- U5 "speech-heads in the weighing … ḏd in red and the name black": verified (weighing units 0, 11, 26).
- U3 "earlier parts code the same figure in Ani's name A51 or A1": verified.
- The title claim (rꜣw nw prt m hrw is the edition's Egyptian title): verified against the published title.
- imḏw units (U10, U13): sound. The l / i gap "[…]" is honest, the sign values im + ḏw are stated as values and not a reading of a known word, Budge's 'advocate' is given only as his guess, and the gloss no longer claims an office.
- ink slip: kept as a slip under the misprints rule (only one reading fits: every other sentence opens with ink, and the man is ink's classifier); the note now admits the repeated writing.

Considered and refused:
- ind (Aa27 nḏ) read ind rather than inḏ: the published hymn to Ra reads the same signs ind with lemma ind and say inedj; kept for consistency.
- kꜣ with D29 phon (published parts have D28 log for kꜣ 'ka'): here the arms write the sound for a different word, 'bull', with the bull classifier, so phon is right.
- ḥḥ with lemma nḥḥ: pass 1's reason (identical to the published hymn to Osiris) stands; the note says the n is not written.
- U5 in 'says' and im·i '(with) me(?)': grammar sound, doubt marked; kept.
- U7/U14 O26 phon ꜥḥꜣ: the codes cannot change and the note marks the reading doubtful; kept.
- U14 sbi 'go': known gloss and signs (walking legs) agree; Budge's 'defeat' is rightly set aside. Kept.
- U12 smꜣ from a written smꜣꜥ: kept as a slip (knife classifier).
- say forms: all match the published parts where the reading recurs (hayt = ḥꜣyt hayt; kheftyu; imentet; inedj; Iunu; Hut-ser); new ones follow the rule.
- No Budge-isms in l / i; "Hail to you" is the known gloss of ind ḥr·k.
- __broaden__ ꜣḫ and ḥr: each keeps the known entry whole, character for character, then " · also …"; the unit gloss overrides match. No lemma in units.json is missing from known-lemmas and gloss.json, and no other broadening is needed (hrw 'day', kꜣ 'bull', in 'say', nn 'these', r 'against', m 'among' are already in known).

Re-check: the concatenated glyph codes of units.json equal the packet's sequence (381 signs), all 106 q values equal the packet's, restored flags stay on the two glyphs of wꜥ (l. 8). The edits were made by script (scratchpad pass2.py), which asserts that codes and q are unchanged.
